title: Implement GitStorageProvider class
description:
Create src/storage/git.ts with GitStorageProvider class:

## Core Functionality
- Extends local storage pattern (uses filesystem for fast I/O)
- Auto-commit: Debounced commit after writes (2s delay)
- Auto-sync: Periodic sync with remote (configurable interval)
- Graceful degradation: Works as local-only if no remote

## Implementation Details
1. Constructor: Accept git provider config, initialize base path
2. write/writeBuffer: Local write + schedule debounced auto-commit
3. startSync(): Begin periodic sync loop (setInterval)
4. stopSync(): Cleanup sync loop for graceful shutdown
5. private autoCommit(): Stage all + commit with configured message
6. private syncWithRemote(): Pull changes, handle conflicts, push if ahead

## Conflict Handling
- Use fast-forward only pulls
- If can't fast-forward, log error (don't lose local changes)
- Expose sync status in getGitStatus()

Import shared utilities from git-utils.ts for all git operations.
close_reason: Implemented GitStorageProvider with auto-commit debouncing and periodic sync.

title: Bibliographies/citations
description:
Glint should support references and citations in a robust manner. A document with references should be able to have the references cited in the body of the text. This should be comparable to bibtex but simpler and in markdown.

One thought is something like:

```markdown

[...]

We can see from [[#ref:foo]] that ...

[...]


## References
  - [ref:foo] "Foo" (2025) http://arxiv.org/abcdefg 
```

When the document is rendered, the reference is rendered as:

```
We can see from [1] that...
```

The user mouses over [1] to see information pulled from the citation (like the full title/authors/abstract)

The design phase consists of:

1. Perform background research on how other people have solved this problem in the context of Markdown-driven document systems.
2. Design the feature, including backend and front end.
3. Critically review and refine the design
4. Issue implementation beads with dependencies

Some thoughts:
- This could be a "widget" like the todo/comment widgets, if it makes sense.
- We will need some LLM instructions (similar to the widgets) that tell agents/llms how to manage references.
- Being compatible with bibtex in some way could be nice but we want to err on the side of simplicity.
close_reason: Design complete, implementation tracked in follow-up beads

title: Journal view
description:
Add a "journal view"

A journal view gathers dated sections together from disparate pages. For example, if the files looked like:

foo.md:
	## 2025-12-31
	...
	## 2025-12-30
	...

bar.md:
	## 2025-12-31
	...
	## 2025-12-29
	...


The journal view would be like:

```
## 2025-12-31

[foo.md]
    ...

[bar.md]
    ...

## 2025-12-30

[foo.md]
    ...

## 2025-12-29

[bar.md]
    ...
```

This is a significant feature, so your job is to:

1. Design the feature and write a design doc
2. Break the implementation down into small tasks
3. Create an `epic` bead for the feature.
3. Create beads for the tasks
4. Create a review bead that is blocked by the implementation tasks and blocks the 'epic' bead

- gitPull(cwd) - Fast-forward pull from origin
- gitPush(cwd, branch) - Push to origin branch
- gitSync(cwd) - Full commit/pull/push cycle
- hasRemote(cwd) - Check if origin remote exists

title: task view that aggregates tasks across pages
description:
We should be able to see a "task view" where all tasks are gathered in one place.
- Tasks that have been completed for > X days (configurable, pick some reasonable default like 7) are hidden
- Design care needed to avoid scanning entire folder every time (caching for unchanged files)
- Interacting with tasks in task view updates source

Some other considerations:
- Should tasks be upgraded to a "plugin" since they have multiple components (widget, state logic, now this view)? should we design a plugin system?
- Should task view be sharable?

Steps:

1. Design this feature. Write a design doc to `docs/`
2. Review and refine the design.
3. Issue implementation beads with dependencies.
4. Issue final "review" bead to review the implementation.
